messages:
jen (support): Hey team, getting a high-severity from an enterprise customer — multiple services throwing 401s in the last 10m after an IdP rotation. Customer says tokens were issued minutes ago and then suddenly failed with 'signature verification failed'.

maria (eng-security): ugh. do we have the kid mismatch/error from their logs? can you paste the raw validation error and the jwt header?

jen (support): pasted from customer logs: `SignatureVerificationError: 'Kid not found'` and a few `Invalid signature` entries. customer also provided the JWT header: `{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"rk-2026-rot-3"}`. They claim the IdP rotated keys ~2m ago.

tom (api-platform): Our JWKS cache TTL is 5m in the runtime, and we have a cold-cache strategy that only refetches on 5xx from jwks endpoint. If IdP rotates and pushes new kid, we might still be using an old key set until TTL expires.

kevin (sre): @idp-team-bot — any rotation events recently?

deploy-bot: IdP rotation event recorded at 1860001120. New key id rk-2026-rot-3 added.

maria (eng-security): that lines up. customer tokens with kid=rk-2026-rot-3 were issued after the rotation but our cache hasn't refreshed, so incoming validation tries old keys -> signature invalid / kid missing.

jen (support): customer provided repro curl against our API:```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InJrLTIwMjYtcm90LTMifQ...." https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate```they get 401 every time.

tom (api-platform): quick repro on my side shows the same for a token with new kid until I `curl https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json` to prime the cache. After that our verifier picks up the new key and accepts the token. So root cause = JWKS caching + rotation without proactive cache invalidation.

maria (eng-security): two related issues: 1) tight coupling of cache TTL and rotation risk, 2) no leeway for clock skew? any 'token expired' noise?

jen (support): some customers also saw `token expired` for tokens issued a few seconds before. logs show validation failure at aud/exp check with difference ~45s. One user in Europe complaining more than US.

kevin (sre): that smells like clock skew between IdP and our validators. We currently accept leeway=10s. increase to 60s? but need to be careful with replay windows.

maria (eng-security): agree, increase to 60s for now while we fix clock sync and issue a config flag. Also implement immediate JWKS refetch on 'kid not found' (not just 5xx). That should reduce impact on rotations.

tom (api-platform): I'll draft a patch: change JWKS cache behavior to: 1) on kid not found -> synchronous refetch and retry validation once, 2) lower default TTL to 90s, 3) add metrics for jwks_refetch_count and jwks_kid_miss. Patch referenced below.

tom (api-platform): patch sketch:```python
# simplified verifier flow
jwks = jwks_cache.get(jwks_url)
try:
    key = jwks.get_key(kid)
except KeyError:
    # immediate refetch on kid miss
    jwks = fetch_jwks(jwks_url, cache_bust=True)
    key = jwks.get_key(kid)  # may raise again -> reject
```

maria (eng-security): also update verifier config to `leeway=60` and add a runtime flag so we can tune per-customer if needed. Add audit logging when we accept with leeway > 10s.

kevin (sre): operationally we should also have an alert on >0.5% auth failures across a 5m window for an org — that will surface rotation-related spikes.

jen (support): customer asks for workaround immediately — can we 1) ask them to reissue tokens? 2) we can prime jwks if they hit us after rotation?

maria (eng-security): best temporary guidance: ask IdP to issue tokens with existing key if possible (rollback), or have them hit our /health/jwks-probe endpoint we've just created (tom) to force cache update. Also request token reissue if feasible. We'll communicate ETA for fix.

tom (api-platform): I've just pushed a hotfix to staging that implements kid-miss refetch + metrics. rolling to prod after smoke. will include a short-circuit: if refetch fails, fall back to old behavior and log detailed context.

deploy-bot: deploy started for api-platform at 1860001380 by tom.

kevin (sre): do we have a repro script to validate fixes? I made this quick script for testing rotation scenarios:```bash
# repro.sh - simulate idp rotation
# 1) fetch current jwks -> save to file
curl -s https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json -o jwks.old
# 2) instruct idp to rotate (manual step /simulate)
# 3) issue token signed with new kid
# 4) hit our endpoint with token -> expect 401 before refetch, 200 after refetch
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_NEW_KID" -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/some-endpoint
```

maria (eng-security): nice. after deploy we'll run it against staging and then prod canary a single org. Also add a unit test for the verifier: simulate kid not found -> ensure fetch_jwks called and retry attempted.

jen (support): customer updated — they can reissue tokens but want a guarantee this won't happen again. I'll tell them we've implemented immediate refetch and increased leeway while we monitor.

kevin (sre): follow-ups: (a) check all components using cached jwks (edge proxies, internal services) and ensure they use same policy, (b) ensure host clocks sync via chrony/ntp and monitor drift, (c) add runbook entry for idp rotations.

maria (eng-security): logging to capture for postmortem: request id, token kid, jwks_cache_age, refetch_attempts, validation_error. Add correlation id when we do refetch.

tom (api-platform): deploying to prod canary now (10% traffic) at 1860001420. I'll post results in 5m.

deploy-bot: canary deployment completed at 1860001445. no regressions on perf tests.

tom (api-platform): canary looks clean; metrics show jwks_refetch_count spike at deploy then steady. acceptance test with repro token passes.

jen (support): customer informed and will validate on their side. keeping ticket open until they confirm. thanks all :pray:

maria (eng-security): filing a short incident note and actions: - change jwks policy globally - add leeway config - runbook for rotations - postmortem if customer impact > 1 org. I'll create the doc.

idp-team-bot: Noted rotation event and team pinged for coordination.

kevin (sre): marking this thread for follow-up in 24h to ensure no further 401 spikes.

jen (support): closing loop for now, will re-open if customer sees more failures.
